title: Loud & Quiet, Fast & Slow
strapline: The whole art of music in two big ideas — how loud, and how fast.
intent: Children explore dynamics and tempo — loud and quiet, fast and slow — the building blocks of expressive music.
Children learn to control the sounds they make deliberately, not just make noise.
Children develop listening and self-regulation as they respond to signals to get louder, softer, faster, stiller.
Children build the vocabulary of music — loud, quiet, fast, slow, getting louder, getting quieter.
Children experience anticipation, control and the fun of stopping and starting together.
implementation: Use voices, instruments or body percussion and play with the volume: whisper it, then shout it, then whisper again.
Introduce a conductor signal — hands high for loud, low for quiet, and a clear 'stop' — and let children lead it.
Play tempo games — sing or play a song slowly like a tortoise, then fast like a hare.
Try 'getting louder / getting quieter' as a wave that swells and fades, so children feel the gradual change.
Add a listening game: play soft and children tiptoe, play loud and they stamp, stop and they freeze.
Feed in the words constantly — loud, quiet, fast, slow — and link them to feelings and pictures.
Keep it playful and let children take the conductor role, giving them real control over the group's sound.
key_questions: Can you make it really quiet? Now really loud?
Shall we play it fast like a hare or slow like a tortoise?
Can you make the sound get louder and louder... then fade away?
What should we do when the music stops?
Can you be the conductor and tell us loud or quiet?

impact.text: Children control loud and quiet in their music-making.
Children play and move at fast and slow tempos.
Children respond to signals, starting and stopping together.
Children use dynamics and tempo vocabulary.
Children self-regulate, listening and controlling their sounds.
Children lead the group as conductor, directing the sound.

enhancements: Volume and tempo picture cards to hold up and 'conduct' with.
A 'musical statues' game linking sound signals to movement.
Recordings that swell and fade to move along with.
Instruments alongside voices so dynamics can be explored both ways.
A story soundtrack — quiet for sleeping, loud for the storm.

playing_exploring: Children explore the full range from whisper to shout.
They test how fast and slow, loud and quiet they can go.
active_learning: Children focus to respond to signals and control their sound.
They relish leading the group and getting it just right.
creating_thinking: Children choose dynamics and tempo to match a feeling or picture.
They direct the group's sound, planning when to swell and fade.
